title: Earthquake
description: Use this list before an earthquake ever happens - there is no warning, so the work is done ahead of time.

items.text: Practice Drop, Cover, and Hold On with everyone in the home (and Lock, Cover, Hold On for wheelchair or walker users) - do not run outside or stand in a doorway
Strap bookcases, cabinets, and other tall furniture to wall studs - falling objects cause most quake injuries
Strap the water heater to wall studs so it cannot tip, break gas lines, or start a fire
Move heavy and breakable items to low shelves; secure TVs, mirrors, and hanging objects away from beds and seats
If you live on the coast, learn your tsunami zone and walking route - strong or long shaking (20+ seconds) is your warning to move to high ground
Keep a flashlight by every bed - power often fails and broken glass is hard to see in the dark
Keep sturdy shoes and work gloves by every bed - broken glass causes many injuries after the shaking
Store water: at least 1 gallon (3.8 L) per person per day, aiming for 2 weeks, in a low, secured spot
Store at least 2 weeks of non-perishable food that needs little or no cooking, plus a manual can opener
Find your gas meter and learn how to shut it off - but only shut it off if you smell gas or hear hissing
Keep the right-size wrench at the gas meter; once off, only the gas company should turn it back on
Keep a fire extinguisher in the kitchen and garage - fires from broken gas lines are common after quakes
Keep extra prescription medicine on hand - ask your doctor and pharmacist how to build a reserve your plan allows
Keep a whistle by each bed and in your kit - if trapped, tap or whistle instead of shouting to save energy and avoid breathing dust
Keep a packed go-bag near an exit or in the car so you can grab it if the building is unsafe to re-enter
Keep a battery or hand-crank radio to get instructions when power, phones, and internet are down
Turn on earthquake alerts on your phone if you live where they are offered (such as the West Coast)
Pick an out-of-area contact and write the number on paper - texts often get through when calls do not
Keep copies of important documents in a waterproof container you can grab quickly
Keep charged power banks (and a small solar charger if you have one) for phones and lights
Review insurance - standard homeowner's policies usually do not cover earthquake damage
Have an older or weak building checked for a seismic retrofit if you own it
